..
Issued at 1235 PM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

High pressure drifting across the Great Lakes area early this
week is bringing northerly flow today (northeasterly tomorrow)
to the Quad State and keeping temperatures fairly cold with
highs in the upper 40s to near 50 and lows primarily in the 20s.

The primary weather concern continues to be the Thanksgiving
system which has a degree of wintry weather with it. The 
synoptic setup is complicated, with two upper level systems 
involved. One of these, located in the Dakotas Tuesday, plunges 
south-southeastward. The second, over Texas, drifts 
northeasterly or east-northeasterly depending on model run. 
Moisture from the Texas system rides northward on the eastern 
side near the Mississippi River, and reaches the Quad State 
Tuesday night into Wednesday. The northern system then pulls 
this moisture more northwestward from Western Kentucky towards 
St Louis and Central Illinois. A few snow flurries may be 
possible early Wednesday morning, but rain is expected through 
the day Wednesday, with a 60-90% chance over all but the Ozark 
Foothills.

Models differ as to whether these two upper lows merge near the
Quad State or stay separated (the southern system tracking
across the Deep South appears to be the more common form of the
latter). The mergers develop a surface low around Kentucky
Thanksgiving Day, but even in many of those model runs a larger
surface low pressure organization appears to develop further 
east near the Atlantic coast.

The more visible deterministic 6z runs did a great job of hyping
up large snowfall totals in our far northwest and areas further
north and will surely be shared repeatedly by folks eager for a
Thanksgiving snowstorm. However, the 6z ensembles and 
subsequent deterministic runs show significant variation in 
models. For instance, the 12z GEFS mean snowfall with this 
event is not quite an inch in the far northwest. The ensemble
members with higher snowfall totals (for some area, not 
specifically the Quad State) are primarily focused on 
development of banded snow in a NW to SE orientation, most of 
which put banded snow north of the Quad State region (but vary 
from near the Mississippi River to east-central Illinois), with
only a few ensemble members including far northwestern portions
of the Quad State in this banding.

Snowfall chances have increased this model cycle, with a 30-70%
chance of minor accumulations (a tenth of an inch of snow or
more) in northwestern portions of the Quad State, with 10-25% 
chances of minor impacts on roads. Western Kentucky, Southwest 
Indiana, and far Southeast Missouri are most likely to be 
limited to a few snow flurries mixing in, if any. Areas from 
Poplar Bluff, MO to Cairo-Harrisburg-Carmi, IL are likely to see
a dusting of snow on grassy surfaces, but travel impacts are 
unlikely. Perryville, MO to Mount Vernon, IL are likely to have 
some snow on grassy surfaces Thanksgiving morning, with some 
potential for travel impacts. Being the busiest travel time of 
the year, look for your winter supplies just in case 
(especially if you/your visitors are going to/traveling from 
locations to the north) and use caution, as the first snowfall 
of the season can be more dangerous. 

Breezy WNW winds are forecast Thanksgiving Day with highs
currently slated to be in the 40s, but there is potential for
these values in particular to lower if there's any snow cover
from Wednesday night. A changeover to rain would clean up any
snow issues on roads. Overall QPF is around a half inch in the
west and an inch in the east, which will provide a little help
for the developing drought. A shift to westerly winds Friday 
and then southwesterly flow for the weekend will allow for a 
warming trend with dry air moving in as the Thanksgiving system 
pushes towards New England.
